intro.title: Compound Component (Tabs)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Tabs component that allows users to switch between different content panels. You will learn the compound component pattern, a React design technique where components work together through implicit state sharing. The main technologies involved are React with TypeScript, using props, children, and context to manage the tab state. By the end, you will create a reusable and flexible Tabs system where the Tab and TabPanel components coordinate without passing props explicitly.
intro.usecase: Compound components like Tabs are fundamental to modern UI design, appearing in dashboards, settings panels, and content-heavy applications. You'll see this pattern in analytics platforms where users switch between different data views, in e-commerce admin panels for managing products/orders/customers, and in documentation sites with code examples in multiple languages. As a developer, you'll implement tabbed interfaces for user profiles, configuration wizards, or any UI where you need to organize related content into distinct, toggleable sections without overwhelming the user.
